The turbine had a chord-to-radius ratio (c/R) of 0.49.
The Reynolds number based on blade chord and freestream velocity was 44,000.
The turbine solidity was 0.16 for the two-bladed configuration and 0.08 for the single-bladed configuration.
The virtual camber of the symmetrical NACA 0018 foil was approximately 6% at infinite tip-speed ratio (λ=∞).
The position of maximum virtual camber shifted from mid-chord towards the leading edge as tip-speed ratio (λ) increased.
For the single-bladed turbine, the negatively cambered (concave-in) blade reduced peak loading by 13% compared to the symmetrical blade.
The URANS simulations suggested that a small but positive total camber (geometric plus virtual) is optimal for this turbine design.
Particle image velocimetry (PIV) was used to explore the near-blade hydrodynamic influences on performance in the upstream and downstream regions of the turbine cycle.
The time-averaged power output was highest for the symmetrical or negatively cambered (concave-in) foils, especially at moderate to low tip-speed ratios.

The positively cambered (concave-out) blade had better upstream performance at lower tip-speed ratios, but this was more than offset by diminished performance in the downstream portion of the rotation.
The optimal tip-speed ratio (λ) for the two-bladed turbine decreased slightly with increased camber, from 2.15 for the negatively cambered blade to 1.98 for the positively cambered blade.
The upstream performance continued to increase past the optimal tip-speed ratio, while the downstream performance degraded quickly at higher rotation rates.
The virtual incidence (α) was approximately 7° and opposed the preset pitch of -6°, resulting in an effective inward pitch of around 1°.
The virtual camber and incidence increased with increasing tip-speed ratio (λ) and approached asymptotic values at high λ.
